title: Teaching at Grunewald School of Music and the GI Bill
summary: Taught trumpet and harmony; veterans received ninety dollars a month.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What was the, I'm trying to think I have a note here. Kind of losing it. So you were, so music was, music was your full time occupation when you came back after the war.

Then I taught, I taught music at the Grunewald School of Music. Oh, Grunewald, okay. That was a school on Camp Street, around Camp and Julia. I taught trumpet over there and taught a harmony. See because the whole while I was in the Navy I did a lot of studying, studying music.
How was, who supported Grunewald? Was it, wasn't it, was it a government program? Yeah. And GI Bill? Yeah.

And guys went on the GI Bill. See the guys who were married, who went to school there, they would get a check every month for ninety dollars. And with like a ninety dollars a month was a lot of money. Some of the guys didn't, they would play a little jobs. Right. But they would, the thing where they really made the income was from going to school. And it was a very good school, they had some good material. Some of the guys didn't go there to learn. They came, they would go there to get that ninety dollars a month. Like I had some trumpet students that didn't want to take the trumpet lessons. They said, man I just signed your slip that I had taken your lessons. I said, but that's not helping you. Well man, I don't feel like practicing it. But then of course there were a lot of good students who went there.
